options.text: A tool for building images faster
Software that manages containers across a cluster of machines — scheduling, scaling, self-healing, and more
A registry for storing images
A way to write Dockerfiles

questions.explanation: An orchestrator runs and manages containers across many machines, handling placement, scaling, self-healing, service discovery, and load balancing.

options.text: You issue step-by-step imperative commands to start each container
You declare the goal (e.g. 5 healthy replicas) and the orchestrator continuously reconciles reality to match it
The orchestrator picks a random number of replicas
You must manually restart failed containers

questions.explanation: Orchestrators are declarative: you state the desired state, and a control loop keeps correcting drift (crashes, node failures) to maintain it.

questions.prompt: Why is plain Docker Compose not a substitute for an orchestrator?

options.text: Compose cannot run more than one container
Compose runs a multi-container app on a single host; it does not spread work across machines or reschedule after a node fails
Compose does not support volumes
Compose cannot use images

questions.explanation: Compose is great for one host, but it does not provide multi-host scheduling, cross-node self-healing, or autoscaling — that is what orchestrators add.

questions.prompt: An orchestrator automatically restarting crashed containers and rescheduling those from failed nodes is called ______. (hyphenated word)
questions.explanation: Self-healing restores the desired state by replacing failed containers and rescheduling workloads from dead nodes onto healthy ones.

questions.prompt: How do Docker Swarm and Kubernetes compare at a high level?

options.text: Swarm is the industry standard; Kubernetes is built into Docker
Swarm is simpler and built into Docker; Kubernetes is more powerful, the industry standard, with a steeper learning curve
They are identical
Neither can self-heal

questions.explanation: Swarm is easy and built into Docker for small clusters; Kubernetes is far more powerful and the industry standard, but more complex.

questions.prompt: Which capabilities do orchestrators typically provide? Select all that apply.

options.text: Scheduling containers onto suitable nodes
Scaling the number of replicas up or down
Service discovery and load balancing across replicas
Writing your application's business logic for you

questions.explanation: Orchestrators schedule, scale, self-heal, and provide service discovery and load balancing. They run your app; they do not write it.
